title: HydroBASINS v1c – Hierarchical Sub-basin Boundaries (Africa, levels 1–12)
description: HydroBASINS is a set of vector polygon layers depicting watershed and sub-basin boundaries globally, derived from HydroSHEDS 15 arc-second hydrography. Twelve hierarchically nested levels with Pfafstetter coding allow up- and downstream topological analysis; versions without lakes ('standard') and with inserted lakes ('customized') are provided per continent.
purpose: Provides consistent catchment and sub-basin units for aggregating rainfall, drought, evapotranspiration and surface-water indicators over Algeria's coastal (Tell) basins, the endorheic High Plateaux chotts and Saharan basins.

spatial_extent.description: Distributed per continent; the Africa file (prefix hybas_af) contains Algeria. The global product covers about 135.0 million km² of land excluding Antarctica. Users must select Algerian basins (note that many basins cross national borders).

temporal_extent.description: Static product derived from SRTM-based HydroSHEDS v1 (SRTM acquired February 2000). Technical documentation v1.c dated July 2014.

resolution.spatial: Vector, derived from 15 arc-second (~500 m) HydroSHEDS grids

variables.name: Hybas_id / Next_down / Next_sink / Main_bas
variables.description: Sub-basin ID and downstream, next-sink and main-basin topology

variables.name: Sub_area / Up_area
variables.description: Sub-basin area and total directly connected upstream area

variables.name: Dist_sink / Dist_main
variables.description: Distance from polygon outlet to next downstream sink / main basin outlet

variables.name: Endo
variables.description: Endorheic indicator: 0 not endorheic, 1 part of an endorheic basin, 2 endorheic sink

variables.name: Coast
variables.description: Lumped coastal basin indicator (0 = no, 1 = yes)

variables.name: Order
variables.description: Classical river order (0 = lumped coastal conglomerates)

variables.name: Lake
variables.description: Customized (with lakes) format only: 0 no lake, 1 lake, 2 reservoir, 3 lagoon

processing: Watersheds were delineated from HydroSHEDS 15 arc-second flow directions and broken down hierarchically following the Pfafstetter concept (nine sub-units per level) over 12 levels. Small coastal basins were lumped into coastal drainage units (up to 500 km²), endorheic basins were grouped and seeded with Pfafstetter codes manually, and some small endorheic sinks were given 'virtual' connections to the surrounding river basin.
limitations: Quality depends on the SRTM-derived HydroSHEDS v1 hydrography; in very flat terrain (e.g. Saharan plains and High Plateaux depressions) drainage divides are less certain.
Small endorheic sinks may be virtually connected to larger basins (Endo = 2 with Next_down > 0); users must decide whether to terminate routing at endorheic sinks.
Small coastal basins are lumped into coastal units up to 500 km², which affects analyses along the Algerian Mediterranean coast.
Pfafstetter coding forces nine sub-basins per level, which can yield irregular sub-basin sizes at some levels.
Attributes are mostly geometric; the licence prohibits redistribution as a stand-alone product.

algeria_notes: Algeria combines short Mediterranean coastal basins in the Tell (lumped into coastal units where small), large endorheic systems on the High Plateaux (chotts) and vast Saharan endorheic or poorly defined drainage. Use the ENDO/NEXT_SINK fields to handle endorheic routing, and expect low-confidence divides in flat desert terrain. For reservoir/dam analyses, basins can be combined with JRC Global Surface Water layers.

verification.notes: The Africa all-levels URL (hybas_af_lev01-12_v1c.zip) is the exact link published on the official page, but could not be confirmed as a file because data.hydrosheds.org serves a Cloudflare bot challenge (HTTP 403) to curl, so download_url is left null and no file size is given. Shapefile format is inferred from the TechDoc file naming (Hybas_XX_levYY_v1c.shp); the page itself only states shapefile for Pour Points. Attribute names follow the TechDoc v1.c field table capitalisation. HydroSHEDS v2 (CC-BY 4.0) includes only a beta HydroBASINS limited to the Americas, so v1c remains the Africa product. Licence restriction on stand-alone redistribution is from Appendix A, section 2.1.2 of the HydroSHEDS TechDoc v1.4.
